summary:
The “Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025” authorizes appropriations for the Department of Defense and military construction for fiscal year 2025 and enacts a broad set of policy reforms. The bill authorizes $167.8 billion for procurement, $14.3 billion for Army research, development, test, and evaluation, $59.0 billion for Army operation and maintenance, and $75.3 billion for Navy operation and maintenance, among other funding.

Servicemember quality of life provisions include new basic pay tables effective April 1, 2025, with caps tied to Executive Schedule levels. Postpartum physical fitness test and body composition assessment deferrals are expanded to cover pregnancy loss and stillbirth. Parental leave is extended to the Coast Guard Reserve, effective October 1, 2025. The cap on additional retired pay for extraordinary heroism is removed for Vietnam-era members. Various bonus and special pay authorities are extended through December 31, 2025. The Army’s operation and maintenance account includes an additional $170.8 million for quality of life initiatives.

Several major weapon system limitations and force structure requirements are imposed. The Secretary of Defense may not accept more than 30 F-35A, 9 F-35B, and 9 F-35C aircraft until certifying that numerous deficiencies—including digital twin models, software integration labs, and sustainment challenges—are being resolved. Construction of the Constellation-class frigate beyond the basic and functional design phase is restricted until 95 percent of design drawings are approved and certified. The Air Force is prohibited from retiring F-15E aircraft until September 30, 2027, with case-by-case exceptions for uneconomical repairs. KC-135 tanker aircraft in the reserve components may not be reduced, and replacement must be on a one-for-one basis unless waived. The Air Force must develop a 10-year tactical fighter force structure plan and report annually. Minimum inventory requirements are adjusted for several aircraft, including reducing the A-10 minimum from 135 to 96. Air base air defense sites must be fielded—at least four by September 30, 2027, and four per year thereafter.

In research and technology, the bill establishes a Chief Digital Engineering Recruitment and Management Officer to define the artificial intelligence workforce and requires AI education courses. Pilot programs are created for AI-driven biotechnology applications, workflow optimization at depots and in contract administration, and a Quantum Benchmarking Initiative at DARPA. An Agility Prime Transition Working Group is formed to accelerate hybrid-electric vertical takeoff and landing capabilities. A Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems Task Force must update guidance for installation commanders within 120 days. The Office of Expanded Competition is established in the Air Force to counter adversarial capital flows. Fundamental research collaboration with certain foreign academic institutions is restricted, subject to a national security waiver.

Space provisions extend the National Security Space Launch program through 2029 and require seven days’ notice before modifying the Phase Three acquisition strategy. A hybrid satellite communication pilot program integrating government and commercial systems is mandated, along with a Middle East space security assessment.

Military construction authorizations are extended for numerous lapsed Guard and Reserve projects. The Naval Innovation Center is authorized at the Naval Postgraduate School. Assistance to Guam regulatory agencies is permitted to expedite construction. A federally funded research and development center must review DoD construction roles and responsibilities.

Homeland security measures include establishment of a DHS Northern Border Mission Center within one year, a government-wide study on security assessments for high-security leased space, and a GAO report on the Homeland Security Information Network. The bill also rescinds $13 million in unobligated balances from railroad unemployment insurance funds.
